F-63ac8dcd767b.text: MRF-L1-O3 (section 2.8): "An unchanged lock gives the pull-request key, which is already saved" -- a scheduled run restores only caches saved on the default branch, so the exact hit comes from the `main` push run's save of the same key. F-f2f1d292ba3b.text: MRF-L2-O1 (section 2.6; CP3): the TLS test needs no certificate. A server that accepts and sends a TLS record header announcing a long handshake record (for example `16 03 03 3f ff`), then trickles single bytes, holds the client inside `do_handshake` past each per-operation timeout. The client verifies nothing until the record completes. That removes the "or else the TLS case is dropped" branch. A silent server would not do: `Deadline.timeout()` sets the per-operation timeout to what remains, so the worker would end by itself and the test would not fail first at 3c7ad52.

F-660d0798de33.text: MRF-L2-O2 (section 2.6): say that the `dup` descriptor is closed once `connect` returns (after the `SSLSocket` is recorded) and on every exit path. F-99d701ac4f7d.text: MRF-L6-O2 (section 2.6; CP3): on expiry, shut down from the caller but close only after the join. Today the caller "shuts down and closes everything recorded, then joins". The recording connection classes override `connect`, so they must still call `_tunnel()` when `_tunnel_host` is set, record the socket before the tunnel's own reads, and record the `dup` before `wrap_socket` as described.
